candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10/PDF p.14: Assess and support client coping, values, beliefs, cultural and spiritual practices; Promote a therapeutic environment
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — spiritual needs, client values, and therapeutic support
candidate.educational_objective: Provide client-centered spiritual care by assessing the client's own spiritual needs, supporting requested resources, and avoiding imposition of the nurse's personal beliefs.

options.A: Tell me what spiritual support would be helpful to you. If you would like, I can help arrange a visit from a chaplain or your own clergy member.
options.B: Spiritual concerns are outside the nursing role, so I will focus only on your physical symptoms.
options.C: I will explain my own religious beliefs so you can decide whether they would help you cope better.
options.D: Spiritual care is appropriate only when the nurse and client share the same religious beliefs.

candidate.rationale: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals describes spiritual assessment and care as open, nonjudgmental, and centered on the client's own values and beliefs. Nurses should ask clients what they need to feel spiritually supported, accommodate requests when possible, and may offer referral to a chaplain or the client's clergy. Nurses should not promote their own beliefs. Therefore A is the best response; B excludes a legitimate nursing-care domain, while C and D substitute the nurse's beliefs for the client's values.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Spiritual care is part of holistic client-centered nursing; nurses assess spiritual needs nonjudgmentally, support the client's own values and beliefs, ask what support is desired, and can offer chaplain or clergy referral while avoiding promotion of their own belief system.
candidate.source_document_title: Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition — Part XVIII Spirituality
candidate.source_locator: Part XVIII > 18.2 Basic Concepts > Spiritual Assessment: ask what provides strength/hope and what spiritual needs can be advocated for; 18.4 Applying the Nursing Process / interventions: ask the client how the nurse can support them spiritually, offer chaplain/clergy resources, and support clients within their own faith tradition without promoting the nurse's beliefs
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf — Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)
candidate.stem: A hospitalized client says, 'My faith has been an important source of strength while I am sick.' Which nursing response best reflects client-centered spiritual care?
